subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt a shared guarded-write/CAS fix for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only repair for this issue?
rationale: The bug affects persisted command-execution approval state and overlaps an open security-sensitive writeback PR, so automation should not choose the permanent write contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt Shared Guarded Write
options.body: Refresh a shared lock/CAS merge primitive on current main and use it for both allow-always persistence and usage metadata writes before closing this issue.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow Allow-Always Repair
options.body: Limit the fix to concurrent allow-always entry persistence if maintainers want to defer broader node metadata writeback security work.

options.title: Wait For Security PR Track
options.body: Keep this issue open until the node stale-writeback PR is landed or replaced, then reassess whether a narrower race remains.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Guarded Write
recommendation.body: Refresh a shared lock/CAS merge primitive on current main and use it for both allow-always persistence and usage metadata writes before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the clearest recent history on exec approval persistence and release state among the likely owners found.
